target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students learning Linear Algebra

sections.title: Introduction: The Quest of Vector Vic
lecture_lines: Meet Vector Vic, a robot on a mission.
He has two movement paths, V1 and V2.
His goal is to reach the target vector B.
How many steps of each path does he take?
We model this quest as a linear system.
animations: A white circle #FFFFFF labeled 'V' representing Vic appears at the origin.
Blue arrow V1 #0000FF and red arrow V2 #FF0000 extend from the origin.
A green arrow B #00FF00 pointing to (7, 11) appears as the target.
Two blue V1 arrows and three red V2 arrows align tip-to-tail to reach B.
White text 'x V1 + y V2 = B' appears at the top, with 'x' and 'y' in yellow #FFFF00.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Determinant as Area
lecture_lines: Start with our two direction vectors, V1 and V2.
They span a parallelogram in the coordinate plane.
This shape's area is the key to our solution.
Algebraically, we call this area the determinant.
For these vectors, the determinant equals five.
animations: Blue vector V1 #0000FF and red vector V2 #FF0000 are shown on a black background.
A yellow parallelogram #FFFF00 at 0.3 opacity forms between V1 and V2.
The area of the parallelogram is labeled 'Area = 5' in yellow #FFFF00.
The boundary vectors V1 and V2 flash white #FFFFFF simultaneously.
Text 'det(V1, V2) = 5' appears below the shape in white #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Vector Combination Problem
lecture_lines: Think of V1 and V2 as a new grid.
Target B sits at a specific spot here.
We need B's coordinates in this custom basis.
animations: The background basis vectors i and j transform into V1 #0000FF and V2 #FF0000.
Target vector B #00FF00 is highlighted at its position relative to the V1-V2 basis.
Coordinates '(2, 3)' appear next to the tip of B in yellow #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Geometric Trick: Replacing a Column
lecture_lines: Look back at our original area of five.
Swap the first vector V1 for target vector B.
This swap creates a brand new green parallelogram.
The new area measures exactly ten units.
The ratio of areas gives us the solution x.
animations: Show the original yellow parallelogram #FFFF00 with area labeled '5'.
The blue vector V1 is removed and replaced by the green vector B #00FF00.
A new green parallelogram #00FF00 forms using B and V2 (red).
The new area is calculated and labeled 'Area = 10' in green #00FF00.
The expression 'x = 10 / 5' appears in white #FFFFFF, then simplifies to 'x = 2'.

sections.title: Shearing and Scaling Logic
lecture_lines: Vector B is made of V1 and V2 parts.
The V2 component shears the shape without changing area.
Only the V1 component determines the area's scale.
animations: Vector B #00FF00 is shown as the vector sum of x*V1 and y*V2 components.
The y*V2 component of the parallelogram (B, V2) slides (shears) along the direction of V2.
A visual indicator shows that the height and base relative to V2 remain unchanged, preserving area.

sections.title: The Formula and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Cramer's Rule uses these area ratios for any variable.
Solving for y, we find a result of three.
Vic follows the paths and reaches his target!
animations: A general mathematical formula for x and y using determinants appears in white #FFFFFF.
Calculation 'y = 15 / 5 = 3' is displayed in red #FF0000 to match the V2 substitution.
Vic moves along the calculated path (2*V1 then 3*V2) to reach the target B.
